headline: Haaland blanks again as Alysson and Barry share the top score
paragraphs: The captaincy went badly for most managers in Gameweek 10. Haaland was the most-captained player for the 10th gameweek in a row, and in 79.5% of squads he scored only 2 points as Man City lost 3-1 at Nott'm Forest. That gave his captains 4 points, and a Triple Captain on him earned just 6. It was his second blank in a row. Delap scored twice for Forest and took 13 points. Among the most-owned players, the best alternative was Groß, whose 10 points would have been worth 20 with the armband. Rogers, in 54.1% of squads, blanked with 2 points.

Man Utd and Aston Villa drew 4-4, and almost nobody had the player who did best out of it. Alysson, owned by 0.1%, scored once and set up two more for 16 points. N.Jackson (11 points) has now scored in three gameweeks in a row and rewarded his 28.5% ownership. Dorgu (11 points) and McGinn (10 points) also reached double figures.
Barry matched that 16-point top score with two goals and an assist as Everton beat Coventry City 3-1. The Everton forward was in 9.0% of squads.

The transfer market was more mixed. Evanilson, the most-bought player with 845,368 net transfers in, scored for the fifth gameweek in a row and took 9 points. João Pedro lost another 1318707 net transfers and then missed a third straight gameweek without playing, even though 34.5% of managers still owned him. The average manager scored 55 points. In a week of 30 goals, the points that counted came from players few people owned.
